tex_content.html:
Definition
[support functions; barrier-sense Hessian and Laplacian bounds]

Source: petersen:page-0296 ↗ lem:pet-ch7-hessian-touching-comparison By subsection 1.3, a $C^2$ function $f:M\to \mathbb {R}$ has $\Hess f|_p\ge B$ for a symmetric bilinear form $B$ on $T_pM$ (respectively $\Delta f(p)\ge a\in \mathbb {R}$) if and only if for every $\varepsilon >0$ there is a function $f_\varepsilon $ defined near $p$, called a support function from below for $f$ at $p$, with

  1. $f_\varepsilon (p)=f(p)$;

  2. $f(x)\ge f_\varepsilon (x)$ near $p$;

  3. $\Hess f_\varepsilon |_p\ge B-\varepsilon g|_p$ (respectively $\Delta f_\varepsilon (p)\ge a-\varepsilon $).

Support functions from above are defined symmetrically and give upper bounds for $\Hess f$ and $\Delta f$. For a merely continuous $f:(M,g)\to \mathbb {R}$ one defines $\Hess f|_p\ge B$ (respectively $\Delta f(p)\ge a$), said to hold in the support or barrier sense, to mean that such smooth support functions $f_\varepsilon $ from below exist for every $\varepsilon >0$. A continuous $f:(M,g)\to \mathbb {R}$ is convex if $\Hess f\ge 0$ everywhere in this sense; this matches the classical definition when $(M,g)\subset (\mathbb {R},g_\mathbb {R})$.
